# OpenMarkdown Editor: full documentation

> Every guide and the API reference of `@openmarkdown-dev/editor`, concatenated. Index: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/llms.txt

# OpenMarkdown Editor

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/

`@openmarkdown-dev/editor` is a live-preview Markdown editor built on [CodeMirror 6](https://codemirror.net/).
Headings, lists, tables, math, Mermaid diagrams, callouts and YAML properties render in place,
and the Markdown shows under the caret. It edits the Markdown source text itself, for a
lossless round-trip: open and save without editing, and the file is byte-for-byte what it was.
When you edit, only what you touched changes, with a few exceptions, each pinned by a test.

It is the editor inside the [OpenMarkdown](https://openmarkdown.dev) app, extracted as an MIT library.

## Start here

1. [Install](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/install/) the package and its CodeMirror peers.
2. [Mount your first editor](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/) in plain JavaScript.
3. Use it [in React](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/) or [in any other framework](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/any-framework/).

## Guides

- [The host: `EditorHost`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/host/): the per-document callbacks (changes, links, images, outline).
- [The environment: `EditorEnvironment`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/): the once-per-page capabilities (color scheme, clipboard, links, spelling, keys).
- [Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/): the `--ome-*` custom properties.
- [UI language](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/language/): English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
- [Images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/): showing, pasting, dropping and resizing.
- [Untrusted content](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/): what the editor does with a document written by someone else.
- [Server-side rendering](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/): importing on the server, mounting in the browser.
- [Self-hosting](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/): building the editor into static files, without a bundler or a CDN, under a strict CSP.

## Fidelity

- [What the editor changes in your file](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/), and what it never changes.
- [How we compared it with other editors](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/method/): method, an example diff, the run date and the caveats.

## Reference and examples

- The [API reference](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/) is generated from the package's type declarations.
- [Examples](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/): small projects you can run, one per task.
- [Live demo](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/demo/): the editor with a showcase document.

## Code and app

The editor's source is in its public repository, and the same editor ships inside the
OpenMarkdown app for macOS, Windows and Linux. To see it with files, folders and an agent
around it, [get the app](https://openmarkdown.dev/#download) or
[try the whole app in your browser](https://openmarkdown.dev/demo).

# Install

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/install/

```sh
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor
```

npm 7 and later also install the editor's **peer dependencies**, CodeMirror and Lezer. With
another package manager, or to pin them yourself, install them explicitly:

```sh
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor @codemirror/state @codemirror/view @codemirror/commands \
  @codemirror/language @codemirror/language-data @codemirror/lang-markdown \
  @codemirror/search @codemirror/autocomplete @lezer/highlight @lezer/markdown
```

## Why peers

Your page must hold exactly one copy of `@codemirror/state`. Two copies break CodeMirror:
extensions from one copy are not recognised by the other ("Unrecognized extension value").
Because CodeMirror is a peer, an app that already uses CodeMirror shares its copy with the
editor.

## What else comes with it

- `temml` (math) and `mermaid` (diagrams) are regular dependencies. The editor loads them
  with `import()` only when a document contains math or a diagram, and your bundler splits
  them into separate chunks. A document without either never downloads them.
- `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` is the same editor without diagram support: nothing
  it imports reaches Mermaid, so your bundler emits no Mermaid chunks, and a ```` ```mermaid ````
  block stays code. It has the same API; import from it instead of the main entry. (npm still
  installs `mermaid`, a dependency of the main entry.)
- There is no CSS file to import. The editor injects its styles, and every color and font is
  a `--ome-*` custom property you can override ([Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/)).

## No bundler?

Framework-free is not build-free. The package is ES modules with bare imports
(`@codemirror/state`, …), which a browser cannot resolve on its own: a page loads it either from
a CDN that rewrites them (once the package is published there) or from files you build once
and serve yourself. [Self-hosting](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/) gives that build, for a
server-rendered app with no bundler or a page that may not use a CDN.

## Requirements

- The package is ES2022 JavaScript with TypeScript declarations included.
- Importing it needs no DOM, so it is safe in server code ([SSR](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/)).
  Mounting an editor needs a browser DOM.
- Every build is tested by mounting, typing, rendering math and a diagram, and switching mode
  and scheme in headless Chromium, WebKit (Safari's engine) and Firefox.

Next: [your first editor](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/).

# Your first editor

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/

Two calls make an editor: `createEditorState` builds one document, and `mountEditor` shows it
in an element. When the document is a file, two more read and write its bytes:

```html
<div id="editor" style="height: 480px"></div>
```

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

let file = openMarkdownFile(new Uint8Array(await (await fetch("/notes.md")).arrayBuffer()));
const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, createEditorState({ doc: file.text }));

const bytes = saveMarkdownFile(editor.getDoc(), file); // write these back
```

Give the parent element a height. The editor fills it and scrolls inside it.

Fetch the file as bytes (`arrayBuffer()`), not as text: `openMarkdownFile` keeps the file's BOM
and line endings, refuses bytes that are not UTF-8, and `saveMarkdownFile` gives back the
original bytes when nothing was edited. Decoding with `response.text()` first would already have
dropped the BOM and the line endings the save needs. See [Fidelity](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/) for what
they keep.

After a save, make the bytes you wrote the new baseline, so that `editor.getDoc() !== file.text`
means "unsaved edits":

```ts
file = openMarkdownFile(bytes);
```

## Read and write the document as a string

When there is no file, only text (a form field, local storage), give the editor a string. It
keeps the document as a string in `\n`, so `editor.getDoc()` is the text.

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc: localStorage.getItem("notes.md") ?? "# Notes\n",
  host: {
    // isUserEdit is false for setDoc and other programmatic changes.
    onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
      if (isUserEdit) localStorage.setItem("notes.md", doc);
    },
  },
});
const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, state);

editor.getDoc(); // the current Markdown, as a string
editor.setDoc("# Replaced\n"); // new text, for example after the file changed on disk; scroll position kept
```

`host` holds the per-document callbacks. Every one is optional; see [the host](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/host/).

## Modes

```ts
editor.setMode("source"); // "live" | "source" | "reading"
editor.mode(); // "source"
editor.view.focus(); // setMode does not move focus
```

- `live` (the default) renders Markdown in place and shows the source under the caret.
- `source` is the plain text, colored.
- `reading` is rendered and read-only.

Switching mode keeps the document, the selection and the undo history. It does not move
focus: when a button of yours calls `setMode`, the focus stays on that button, so call
`editor.view.focus()` afterwards if the user should be able to type right away. To start in
another mode, pass `mode` to `createEditorState`.

## Once per page: the environment

Window-wide capabilities, such as the color scheme, the clipboard and the UI language, are set
once, before the first editor mounts:

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const media = matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
configureEditorEnvironment({
  language: "en",
  colorScheme: {
    current: () => (media.matches ? "dark" : "light"),
    subscribe: (cb) => {
      const on = () => cb(media.matches ? "dark" : "light");
      media.addEventListener("change", on);
      return () => media.removeEventListener("change", on);
    },
  },
  copyText: (text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text),
});
```

Without it the editor is light, English, and has no clipboard, external-link or spelling
behaviour. See [the environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/).

## Clean up

```ts
editor.destroy(); // when the editor leaves the page
```

`destroy` removes the view and stops following the color scheme.

## Several documents in one view

One state is one document, with its undo history, folds and mode. A host with several
documents (tabs, for example) can keep one state each and swap them into one view:

```ts
editor.view.setState(otherState);
editor.syncAmbient(); // re-apply the current light or dark scheme
```

Next: [React](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/), or [any other framework](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/any-framework/).

# Use it in React

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/

There is no React wrapper to install. Mount the editor in an effect, and destroy it in the
effect's cleanup:

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type MarkdownEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

export function MarkdownField({ value, onChange }: { value: string; onChange: (doc: string) => void }) {
  const parent = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const editor = useRef<MarkdownEditor | null>(null);
  const latest = useRef(onChange);
  latest.current = onChange;

  useEffect(() => {
    const state = createEditorState({
      doc: value,
      host: { onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => isUserEdit && latest.current(doc) },
    });
    editor.current = mountEditor(parent.current!, state);
    return () => editor.current?.destroy();
    // Mount once; later `value` changes are pushed in below.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (editor.current && editor.current.getDoc() !== value) editor.current.setDoc(value);
  }, [value]);

  return <div ref={parent} style={{ height: 480 }} />;
}
```

## Why it is written this way

- **Mount once.** Rebuilding the editor on every render would lose the caret, the selection
  and the undo history. The effect has no dependencies, and later `value` changes go in through
  `setDoc`.
- **Callbacks through a ref.** The editor reads `host` through the object on every call, so
  you can mutate it, or read the latest props through a ref as above, without rebuilding the
  state.
- **Only user edits go up.** `setDoc` is not a user edit, so `isUserEdit` keeps a `value`
  pushed in from props from being echoed back to `onChange`.
- **Strict Mode** runs the effect twice in development. `destroy` in the cleanup removes the
  first editor before the second mounts.

## Next.js and other server renderers

Importing the package on the server is safe, and the effect only runs in the browser, so the
component above works in a server-rendered page as it is. See [SSR](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/).

# Use it in any framework

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/any-framework/

The editor is plain TypeScript and DOM. Any framework that gives you an element after it is in
the page, and a hook for when it leaves, can host it. The pattern is always the same:

1. When the element is mounted, call `createEditorState` and `mountEditor`.
2. When the element is removed, call `editor.destroy()`.
3. Send changes up from `host.onChange`. Push outside changes in with `editor.setDoc`, only when
   they differ from `editor.getDoc()`.

## Vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, onBeforeUnmount, ref, watch } from "vue";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type MarkdownEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const props = defineProps<{ modelValue: string }>();
const emit = defineEmits<{ "update:modelValue": [doc: string] }>();
const el = ref<HTMLDivElement>();
let editor: MarkdownEditor | null = null;

onMounted(() => {
  const state = createEditorState({
    doc: props.modelValue,
    host: { onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => isUserEdit && emit("update:modelValue", doc) },
  });
  editor = mountEditor(el.value!, state);
});
watch(() => props.modelValue, (doc) => {
  if (editor && editor.getDoc() !== doc) editor.setDoc(doc);
});
onBeforeUnmount(() => editor?.destroy());
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" style="height: 480px" />
</template>
```

## Svelte

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from "svelte";
  import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

  export let doc = "";
  let el: HTMLDivElement;

  onMount(() => {
    const editor = mountEditor(el, createEditorState({
      doc,
      host: { onChange: (next, isUserEdit) => { if (isUserEdit) doc = next; } },
    }));
    return () => editor.destroy();
  });
</script>

<div bind:this={el} style="height: 480px"></div>
```

## Web component

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type MarkdownEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

class MarkdownEditorElement extends HTMLElement {
  private editor: MarkdownEditor | null = null;

  connectedCallback() {
    const state = createEditorState({
      doc: this.textContent ?? "",
      host: {
        onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
          if (isUserEdit) this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("change", { detail: doc }));
        },
      },
    });
    this.textContent = "";
    this.editor = mountEditor(this, state);
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.editor?.destroy();
    this.editor = null;
  }
}
customElements.define("markdown-editor", MarkdownEditorElement);
```

## A plain `<script>` tag

Without a bundler, load the package and its peers from a CDN that resolves bare imports, for
example [esm.sh](https://esm.sh):

```html
<div id="editor" style="height: 480px"></div>
<script type="module">
  import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "https://esm.sh/@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

  mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor"), createEditorState({ doc: "# Hello\n" }));
</script>
```

# The host: `EditorHost`

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/host/

`EditorHost` is what the editor calls back into, for one document. Pass it as `host` to
`createEditorState`. Every callback is optional: leave one out and that feature is switched off
quietly. Nothing errors, and the rest of the editor carries on.

```ts
import { createEditorState, type EditorHost } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const host: EditorHost = {
  onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
    if (isUserEdit) save(doc);
  },
  resolveImage: (src) => (src.startsWith("https://") ? src : null),
};
const state = createEditorState({ doc, docPath: "/notes/today.md", host });
```

| Callback | Called when | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onChange(doc, isUserEdit, docPath)` | The document changed. `isUserEdit` is false for `setDoc` and other programmatic changes. | Nothing happens. |
| `resolveImage(src)` | An image is shown. Return a URL the page may load, or `null` to show the source. Script-capable URLs are dropped whatever you return. | Only absolute `https:` images load, from any host. Pass `() => null` to load none ([images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/)). |
| `openLink(absPath, fragment)` | A link to a local file was followed (Cmd/Ctrl+click; a plain click in reading mode). `fragment` is its `#fragment` without the `#`, or `null`. | Local links do nothing. |
| `getFolder()` | Link completion needs the root of the user's files. | Completion uses the document's own directory. |
| `listFiles(root)` | Link completion lists linkable files under `root` (root-relative paths). | Completion offers headings only. |
| `saveAttachment(docPath, bytes, hint)` | An image is pasted or dropped. Store it and resolve the relative path to link, or `null`. | Pasting or dropping an image inserts nothing. |
| `onUnsupportedPaste(reason, count)` | Images were pasted or dropped but could not be stored: `reason` is `"no-save-attachment"` or `"no-doc-path"`. A notice only; nothing was inserted. | The images are dropped silently. |
| `onMoved()` | The selection or scroll position moved (debounced). Use it to remember the position. | Nothing happens. |
| `onOutline(items)` | The heading outline changed (`OutlineItem[]`, or `null` when the view goes away). | Nothing happens. |

## The host is read on every call

The editor keeps the object, not its functions, and reads the member each time it needs one.
You can mutate the object after creating the state, or forward to the latest props through a
ref ([React](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/)), without rebuilding the state.

## `docPath`

`docPath` is the document's absolute path, or `null` for an unsaved document. Relative links and
image paths resolve against its directory, and `saveAttachment` is only called when there is a
path to store beside. Change it after a rename with `editor.setDocPath(path)`; read it with
`editor.docPath()`.

The path does not have to be a file on disk. A web app can use any absolute, `/`-separated name
(for example `/doc.md`) and resolve images in `resolveImage` from its own storage. See
[Images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/).

## Reading and writing the file

The editor works on a string; the file on disk is bytes. Decode it with `openMarkdownFile` and
encode `editor.getDoc()` with `saveMarkdownFile`, typically in `onChange` or on a save command:

```ts
import { createEditorState, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const file = openMarkdownFile(bytes); // throws InvalidUtf8Error for a file that is not UTF-8
const state = createEditorState({
  doc: file.text,
  host: {
    onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
      if (isUserEdit) writeFile(saveMarkdownFile(doc, file));
    },
  },
});
```

Unedited, the bytes written are the bytes read; edited, the file keeps its BOM and its dominant
line ending. See [Fidelity](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/).

## Window-wide capabilities live elsewhere

The color scheme, the clipboard, external links, spelling, the UI language and host key
bindings are the same for all editors on the page. They are set once with
`configureEditorEnvironment`: see [the environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/).

The full signatures are in the [API reference](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorhost/).

# The environment: `EditorEnvironment`

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/

Some capabilities belong to the page, not to a document: the color scheme, the clipboard,
external links, spelling, the UI language and the host's key bindings. Provide them once with
`configureEditorEnvironment`, before the first editor mounts. A later call replaces the whole
environment.

Every member is optional. Without the call, the editor is light, English, and has no clipboard,
external-link, spelling or host-key behaviour.

| Member | What it does | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | The editor's own UI words: `"en"`, `"zh"`, `"ja"` or `"ko"`. | English. |
| `colorScheme` | `{ current(), subscribe(cb) }`: the page's `"light"` / `"dark"` scheme and its changes. | Always light. |
| `copyText(text)` | Put text on the clipboard (the code-block copy button). | No copy button action. |
| `openExternal(url)` | A web link was followed (Cmd/Ctrl+click; a plain click in reading mode). Your policy decides how it opens. | Web links do nothing. |
| `refusedLink(url, scheme)` | The editor refused a script-capable link (`javascript:`, `data:` and similar). Use it to tell the user. Never open the URL. | The refusal is silent. |
| `spell` | A `SpellService` that draws spelling squiggles and offers suggestions. | No spell checking. |
| `handleKey(view, event)` | Sees each key before the editor's defaults. Return `true` to consume it. | The editor's keymap only. |

## Follow the system color scheme

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const media = matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
configureEditorEnvironment({
  colorScheme: {
    current: () => (media.matches ? "dark" : "light"),
    subscribe: (cb) => {
      const on = () => cb(media.matches ? "dark" : "light");
      media.addEventListener("change", on);
      return () => media.removeEventListener("change", on);
    },
  },
  copyText: (text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text),
  openExternal: (url) => window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener"),
});
```

A mounted editor subscribes while it lives and unsubscribes in `destroy`. A page with its own
theme toggle implements `colorScheme` over that toggle instead.

## Spelling: `SpellService`

The editor draws its own spelling squiggles and suggestion menu; the checking is yours. A
`SpellService` has six members:

| Member | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `isOn()` | Is spell checking on right now? |
| `onChange(cb)` | Follow the on / off state. Returns the unsubscribe. |
| `newDocument()` | A fresh spell-document number for one editor, so a checker can keep per-editor ignore lists. |
| `check(doc, paragraphs)` | The misspellings (`SpellMiss`, UTF-16 `from` / `to` offsets) for each paragraph, in order, or `null` when the check could not run. |
| `suggestions(doc, paragraph, from, to)` | Up to five suggestions for `paragraph.slice(from, to)`. |
| `closeDocument(doc)` | The editor of `doc` is gone. |

Pass `checkSpelling: false` to `createEditorState` for an editor that should never show
squiggles, such as a small comment box.

## Host key bindings

`handleKey` sees every key the editor's keymap sees, before CodeMirror's defaults. Return `true`
when your binding ran:

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

configureEditorEnvironment({
  handleKey: (view, event) => {
    if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key === "s") {
      save(view.state.doc.toString());
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  },
});
```

The full signatures are in the [API reference](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorenvironment/).

# Theming

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/

The editor paints only with `--ome-*` custom properties. Each one has a light and a dark
default, and the editor switches between them with the environment's `colorScheme`
([environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/)). There is no CSS file to import.

To restyle the editor, set the properties **on `.cm-editor`**:

```css
.cm-editor {
  --ome-bg: #fffdf7;
  --ome-accent: #0b6bcb;
  --ome-font: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

Setting them on `:root` has no effect. The editor declares its defaults on its own root at
zero specificity, so any selector that targets `.cm-editor` wins, and an inherited value does
not.

## Light and dark

The editor's root carries `data-ome-scheme="light"` or `data-ome-scheme="dark"`, and it changes
when the environment's `colorScheme` does. Give each scheme its own values with that attribute:

```css
.cm-editor[data-ome-scheme="light"] { --ome-accent: #0b6bcb; }
.cm-editor[data-ome-scheme="dark"] { --ome-accent: #6cb6ff; }
```

This attribute is the one supported way to tell the schemes apart. CodeMirror's own light and dark
classes are generated names that change between builds, so do not select on them.

## Tokens

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--ome-bg` | The document surface: the editor's background. |
| `--ome-fg` | Body text and the caret: the editor's text color. |
| `--ome-muted` | Quiet surfaces. |
| `--ome-muted-fg` | Secondary text: Markdown marks, placeholders, resting controls. |
| `--ome-border` | Hairlines: table rules, quote bars, frames. |
| `--ome-accent` | Links, selection, find hits, focus, list marks. |
| `--ome-danger` | Errors, such as a search with no match. |
| `--ome-agent` | The `@agent` mention. |
| `--ome-spelling` | The spelling squiggle. |
| `--ome-code-bg` | Inline code, code blocks, table headers (translucent). |
| `--ome-callout-note`, `--ome-callout-tip`, `--ome-callout-important`, `--ome-callout-warning`, `--ome-callout-caution` | The five callout kinds. |
| `--ome-state-hover`, `--ome-state-selected` | Hover and selected layers on controls. |
| `--ome-radius` | The corner radius of controls. |
| `--ome-font`, `--ome-font-mono` | The prose and code font stacks. No font files are shipped. |
| `--ome-syntax-keyword`, `--ome-syntax-string`, `--ome-syntax-number`, `--ome-syntax-function`, `--ome-syntax-type`, `--ome-syntax-property` | Code highlighting. One value is used for both schemes. |

## Size

The editor fills its parent and scrolls inside it, so give the parent a height. Text is 16px at
the editor's root, and every size inside the document is relative to it.

## Beyond tokens

Anything the tokens do not cover can be styled with CodeMirror's own theme extensions, passed
through `extensions` on `createEditorState`. Class names inside the editor are not part of the
public API and may change between versions; the tokens are.

# UI language

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/language/

The editor draws a few words of its own: the find panel, the copy and fold buttons, the
properties block, and image and link chips. They ship in four languages:

| Code | Language |
| --- | --- |
| `"en"` | English (the default) |
| `"zh"` | Chinese (Simplified) |
| `"ja"` | Japanese |
| `"ko"` | Korean |

Choose one with the environment, before the first editor mounts:

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

configureEditorEnvironment({ language: "ja" });
```

- The editor does not guess from the browser. Without `language`, or with a code it does not
  ship, it speaks English, so it behaves the same in every host and your app stays the one place
  that decides the language.
- The language is read when a word is drawn. Words already on screen do not redraw when you call
  `configureEditorEnvironment` again; mount the editor again (or reload) to switch a live page.
- Your document text can be in any language. Only the editor's own controls are translated.
  CJK text and emoji are edited and measured as written (table columns count them as two
  columns wide).

# Images

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/

The editor shows Markdown images (`![alt](src)`) in place, lets the user paste or drop new ones,
and resizes them with a drag. Where image bytes come from and where they go is the host's
decision, through two `EditorHost` callbacks.

## Showing images: `resolveImage`

`resolveImage(src)` gets the image target exactly as written and returns a URL the page may load,
or `null` to show the source text instead.

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc,
  docPath: "/notes/today.md",
  host: {
    resolveImage: (src) => {
      if (src.startsWith("https://")) return src;
      return `/files/notes/${src.replace(/^\.\//, "")}`; // your server serves the document's folder
    },
  },
});
```

- Without `resolveImage`, absolute `https:` images load, from any host, and nothing else does.
  The browser fetches them when the document is shown, which tells their server the document
  was opened. For private documents, pass a `resolveImage` that allows only your own hosts, or
  turn remote images off entirely:

  ```ts
  createEditorState({ doc, host: { resolveImage: () => null } }); // no image loads; the source shows
  ```

- Whatever you return, script-capable URLs (`javascript:` and similar) are dropped. See
  [Untrusted content](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/).

## Pasting and dropping: `saveAttachment`

When the user pastes or drops an image, the editor calls
`saveAttachment(docPath, bytes, hint)` with the image bytes and a file-name hint. Store the bytes
and resolve the document-relative path to link; the editor inserts an image link to that path
where the image was pasted or dropped, with the caret in its alt text.
Resolve `null` when the save failed; the editor inserts nothing (report the failure yourself).

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const urls = new Map<string, string>();
let n = 0;

const state = createEditorState({
  doc: "",
  docPath: "/draft.md", // paste and drop need a document path
  host: {
    saveAttachment: async (_docPath, bytes, hint) => {
      const name = `attachments/pasted-${++n}.png`;
      urls.set(name, URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes.slice()], { type: "image/png" })));
      return name;
    },
    resolveImage: (src) => urls.get(src) ?? (src.startsWith("https://") ? src : null),
  },
});
```

This keeps images in the browser tab only. A real app uploads the bytes and returns the path or
URL it stored them under.

`resolveImage` may be called more than once for the same image, so keep it free of side
effects. When its answer changes, for example after the reader allows remote images, call
`editor.refreshImages()` and every image is resolved again, including those in tables.

- Without `saveAttachment`, pasting or dropping an image inserts nothing.
- With `docPath` set to `null` (an unsaved document), there is nowhere to store beside, so the
  editor does not call `saveAttachment`.
- In both cases the editor stays silent. To tell the user, pass `onUnsupportedPaste`: it is
  called with the reason (`"no-save-attachment"` or `"no-doc-path"`) and how many images were
  dropped.

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc,
  host: {
    onUnsupportedPaste: (reason, count) => {
      showToast(`${count} image(s) not added: this editor cannot store images.`);
    },
  },
});
```
- `hint` is the file's name, or its MIME type when it has no name. It is a hint, not a checked
  type: look at the bytes before you store or serve them.

## Resizing

Every image has a grip in its corner. Dragging it resizes the image, and on release the editor
writes the width into the alt text as `|W`:

```md
![diagram|320](diagram.png)
```

Only that width changes in the file. In reading mode the grip is hidden.

# Untrusted content

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/

The editor is built to render documents written by someone else, such as a teammate or an AI
agent. Rendering a document never runs its script:

- **Raw HTML is shown as source**, never rendered.
- **Math** (Temml, `trust: false`) and the editor's icons reach the DOM only through one sanitiser
  with an allowlist of elements and attributes. Unknown elements make the formula fall back to
  its source. Unknown attributes are dropped.
- **Mermaid** runs with `securityLevel: "strict"` and no HTML labels. Its SVG goes through the same
  allowlist.
- **Links** are classified the way a browser reads them, after decoding entities and removing
  control characters. `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `livescript:` and `data:` links are never passed
  to `openLink` or `openExternal`, however they are obfuscated. Your `refusedLink` is told
  instead.
- **Images**: without a `resolveImage`, only absolute `https:` images load. With one,
  script-capable URLs are still dropped.

## What stays your job

- **Network policy.** An `https:` image in a document is loaded by the browser, which tells its
  server the page was opened. If that matters, return `null` from `resolveImage` for hosts you do
  not trust, or proxy images.
- **Opening links.** `openExternal` and `openLink` receive URLs and paths the editor already
  classified as safe to follow; your policy still decides whether and how to open them.
- **Content Security Policy.** CodeMirror injects `<style>` elements, so a strict `style-src`
  needs a nonce through CodeMirror's `EditorView.cspNonce`, passed with `extensions`:

```ts
import { EditorView } from "@codemirror/view";
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({ doc, extensions: EditorView.cspNonce.of(nonce) });
```

What a strict policy (`script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'`, no `'unsafe-inline'`)
needs, exactly:

- **The editor and math**: only that nonce. The editor writes no `style` attribute; a formula's
  styles are applied through `element.style`, which the policy allows.
- **Diagrams**: more. Mermaid draws each diagram once in the page to measure it, with `style`
  attributes and `<style>` elements that carry no nonce. Without
  `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` and `style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` the browser
  blocks them and reports violations. Either add those two directives, or pass
  `diagrams: false` to `createEditorState` (or import `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams`,
  which leaves Mermaid out of the build): `mermaid` blocks then stay code and Mermaid is
  never loaded. [Self-hosting](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/#diagrams-and-the-policy) gives both policies,
  tested in a browser.

## Known advisories

`npm audit` reports one advisory in a fresh install; npm counts it as `3 low severity
vulnerabilities`, one for each package on the path (`katex`, `mermaid` and this package). We
assessed it, and it does not apply to the editor:

- **GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7** (low; `katex`, installed through `mermaid` 11.17.2): "KaTeX: Existing
  prototype pollution can bypass trust restrictions". Exploiting it needs a prototype pollution
  already present in the page *and* KaTeX output inserted without sanitising. The editor renders
  math with Temml, not KaTeX. Mermaid runs with `htmlLabels: false`, so its labels are plain SVG
  text. Every piece of markup the editor inserts goes through its one sanitiser, which refuses
  anything outside its allow-list. The fix exists only in Mermaid 12, which adds a dependency
  under a license this package cannot take (EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0). With the `no-diagrams` entry,
  neither Mermaid nor KaTeX reaches your bundle. Next review: 2027-02-04.

The release check fails on any advisory that is not assessed here.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately through the repository's GitHub security advisories, not in a
public issue.

# Server-side rendering

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/

Importing `@openmarkdown-dev/editor` does not touch `window` or `document`, so the package can be
imported by code that also runs on the server (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro and the like).
Every build checks this by importing the package in plain Node.

Mounting needs a DOM. Create and mount the editor only in browser code: an effect, an
`onMounted` hook, a client-only component.

```tsx
"use client";
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

export function Editor({ doc }: { doc: string }) {
  const el = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const editor = mountEditor(el.current!, createEditorState({ doc }));
    return () => editor.destroy();
    // Mount once; see the React guide for pushing later changes in.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);
  return <div ref={el} style={{ height: 480 }} />;
}
```

## What the server can render

The server renders the empty parent element. If the page should show the document before the
script runs, render it yourself (as preformatted text or with any Markdown renderer) inside the
parent and clear it when the editor mounts.

## Bundle splitting

Math (Temml) and diagrams (Mermaid) are loaded with `import()` the first time a document shows
math or a diagram. Your bundler splits them into separate chunks; neither is in the first load
of a page whose documents have none.

# Self-hosting

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/

This guide is for pages that load JavaScript as plain files from their own server: a
server-rendered app (Jinja, ERB, Go templates, PHP) with no bundler of its own, or a site whose
policy rules out a CDN. You build the editor once with [esbuild](https://esbuild.github.io/),
copy the output next to your other static files, and load it with one `<script type="module">`
under a strict Content Security Policy.

If your app already has a bundler (Vite, webpack, Rollup, esbuild), you do not need this page:
import the package as in [your first editor](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/) and your
bundler does the same splitting.

## 1. Install

In a small build project (it can live inside your app's repository), install the editor, its
CodeMirror peers and esbuild:

```sh
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor @codemirror/state @codemirror/view @codemirror/commands \
  @codemirror/language @codemirror/language-data @codemirror/lang-markdown \
  @codemirror/search @codemirror/autocomplete @lezer/highlight @lezer/markdown
npm install --save-dev esbuild
```

To build from a local package file instead of the registry (a tarball made with `npm pack`,
for example before a release reaches npm), install the file by its path. npm 7 and later install
the peers listed above with it:

```sh
npm install ./openmarkdown-dev-editor-0.1.0.tgz
npm install --save-dev esbuild
```

## 2. The entry

One module of your own imports the editor and mounts it. It reads the document from a
`<textarea>` your template fills, copies the document back into it on each change (so an
ordinary form post saves it), and hands CodeMirror the page's style nonce:

```js selfhost-entry
// src/editor.js
import { EditorView } from "@codemirror/view";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

// The nonce the server put in this response's CSP header, read from the page.
const nonce = document.querySelector('meta[property="csp-nonce"]')?.nonce ?? "";
const source = document.getElementById("editor-doc");

mountEditor(
  document.getElementById("editor"),
  createEditorState({
    doc: source.value,
    extensions: EditorView.cspNonce.of(nonce),
    // Render ```mermaid blocks as diagrams. Set false to keep them as code and
    // never load Mermaid; see "Diagrams and the policy" below.
    diagrams: true,
    host: { onChange: (doc) => { source.value = doc; } },
  }),
);
```

## 3. The build

This script is the whole build. Run it with `node build.mjs`; it writes the editor into
`static/editor/`:

```js selfhost-config
// build.mjs
import { build } from "esbuild";
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const outdir = "static/editor";

const result = await build({
  entryPoints: ["src/editor.js"],
  bundle: true,
  format: "esm",
  // Mermaid, Temml and each code language become chunks, fetched only when needed.
  splitting: true,
  outdir,
  entryNames: "[name]",
  chunkNames: "chunks/[name]-[hash]",
  target: "es2022",
  minify: true,
  // Keep /*! … */ and @license comments in the file they came from.
  legalComments: "eof",
  metafile: true,
  logLevel: "warning",
});

// Every package that went into the output, with its license text, in one file.
const notices = new Map();
for (const input of Object.keys(result.metafile.inputs)) {
  const dir = /^(.*node_modules\/(?:@[^/]+\/)?[^/]+)\//.exec(input)?.[1];
  if (!dir || notices.has(dir) || !existsSync(join(dir, "package.json"))) continue;
  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, "package.json"), "utf8"));
  const file = readdirSync(dir).find((f) => /^(licen[cs]e|copying|notice)/i.test(f));
  const text = file ? readFileSync(join(dir, file), "utf8") : `License: ${pkg.license}`;
  notices.set(dir, `${pkg.name}@${pkg.version}\n\n${text.trim()}\n`);
}
const all = [...notices.values()].sort();
writeFileSync(join(outdir, "THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt"), all.join(`\n${"-".repeat(72)}\n\n`));
```

- `format: "esm"` with `splitting: true` keeps the editor's lazy `import()`s as separate files.
  Without splitting, esbuild would inline Mermaid and every language into one large file that
  every page downloads.
- `legalComments: "eof"` keeps the license comments some packages put in their code. Most
  packages do not, so the script also writes `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` with the license file of
  every package in the output. Serve it, or link it from your app's notices page: the MIT and
  similar licenses require the notice to travel with the code.

## 4. What it writes

```text
static/editor/
├── editor.js                  the entry: the editor, CodeMirror and Lezer
├── THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt   the license of every package in the output
└── chunks/
    ├── chunk-….js             code shared between the entry and lazy chunks
    ├── mermaid.core-….js      Mermaid, loaded on the first diagram
    ├── flowDiagram-….js       one chunk per Mermaid diagram type (and so on)
    ├── temml-….js             Temml, loaded on the first formula
    ├── dist-….js              a CodeMirror language package
    └── ruby-….js, shell-….js  a legacy-mode language, one per language
```

**Deploy every file.** The entry and the chunks find each other by relative URL, and which
chunks a page needs depends on the documents it opens: a diagram type or a code language no
one has used yet still has to be there the day someone uses it. Copy the whole directory,
never a selection, and copy it again on every upgrade (the hashes in the chunk names change).

## 5. The page

The server makes a fresh nonce for every response, sends it in the CSP header and writes it
into the page. This is the strict policy. It is all the editor, its icons and its formulas
need; with `diagrams: false` in the entry it is all the page needs:

```text selfhost-csp
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-{{ nonce }}'; img-src 'self' https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'
```

A page that renders diagrams uses this one instead (see
[diagrams and the policy](#diagrams-and-the-policy)):

```text selfhost-csp-diagrams
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-{{ nonce }}'; img-src 'self' https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'
```

```html selfhost-page
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>Notes</title>
    <meta property="csp-nonce" nonce="{{ nonce }}" />
    <style nonce="{{ nonce }}">
      #editor { height: 480px; }
    </style>
    <script type="module" src="/static/editor/editor.js"></script>
  </head>
  <body>
    <form method="post">
      <div id="editor"></div>
      <textarea id="editor-doc" name="doc" hidden>{{ doc }}</textarea>
      <button>Save</button>
    </form>
  </body>
</html>
```

- `script-src 'self'` is enough for scripts: the editor and all its chunks are files from your
  origin, and it runs no inline script and no `eval`.
- `style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'`: CodeMirror and the editor inject their styles as `<style>`
  elements, and `EditorView.cspNonce` stamps the nonce on them. The editor writes no `style`
  attribute: what a formula needs is applied through `element.style`, which the policy allows.
  Your own inline `<style>` needs the same nonce; `style="…"` attributes in your template are
  blocked by this policy, so put such rules in a stylesheet.
- `img-src https:` lets documents show images from the web. Narrow it, or drop it and pass a
  `resolveImage` to the host (see [images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/) and
  [untrusted content](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/)).
- The nonce sits on a `<meta>` element's `nonce` attribute rather than in its `content`, the
  same convention as Vite's: the browser hides the attribute from selectors, and the script
  reads it from the `nonce` property.
- Your template engine must escape the document it writes into the `<textarea>` (Jinja's
  autoescape does). Serve `.js` files as `text/javascript`.

## Diagrams and the policy

The editor puts a diagram on the page without inline styles: its `<style>` gets the nonce and
its style attributes are applied through `element.style`. Mermaid itself does not. To measure
a diagram, it draws it once in the page, setting `style` attributes and adding `<style>`
elements that carry no nonce. Under the strict policy the browser blocks those and reports
each one as a violation (about 36 for a flowchart). The diagram still appears, but its text may
be measured without its font settings.

Pick one:

- **Render diagrams**: send the diagram policy above. It is the strict policy plus
  `style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` and `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`. A nonce cannot
  cover Mermaid's `<style>` elements, and browsers ignore `'unsafe-inline'` in a directive that
  also has a nonce, so `style-src-elem` lists none. Inline styles are then allowed on the
  page; scripts stay `'self'` only.
- **No diagrams**: set `diagrams: false` in the entry and keep the strict policy. A
  ```` ```mermaid ```` block shows as code, and the page never fetches Mermaid (its chunks are
  still in the output, unused).
- **No diagrams, and no Mermaid in the build**: import from the package's diagram-free entry
  instead, and keep the strict policy. Change one line of the entry, and drop `diagrams` (that
  entry ignores it):

  ```js
  import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams";
  ```

  `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` is the same editor with the same API, built from the
  same code, minus the diagram support: nothing it imports reaches Mermaid, so esbuild writes no
  Mermaid chunk and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` does not list it. A ```` ```mermaid ```` block
  shows as code. npm still installs the `mermaid` package (it is a dependency of the main
  entry); it just never reaches your output.

## Native WebViews and static hosts

A desktop or mobile app that shows the editor in a WebView (WKWebView, WebView2, Android
WebView), or a site served as static files, has no server to template a page per response.
The build above is the same; four things differ.

- **Serve the files from an origin.** Module scripts and their chunk imports do not load from
  `file://`. Serve the output through a custom scheme (`WKURLSchemeHandler`,
  `WebResourceRequested`, `WebViewAssetLoader`) or a local origin, with `.js` as
  `text/javascript`. Chunk imports are relative, so they resolve against that origin.
- **Wait for the page, not for the load event.** A WebView can report the page loaded before
  the module graph has run, so the first call from native code finds nothing to call. Send a
  message as the entry's last statement and call into the page only after it arrives:

  ```js
  // last line of entry.js (WKWebView; use your WebView's bridge)
  window.webkit?.messageHandlers?.editor?.postMessage({ type: "ready" });
  ```

- **The nonce needs a server.** A nonce only protects a page when it is new for every response;
  a fixed one written into a static file protects nothing. Without a server, use
  `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` (what diagrams need anyway), keep `script-src 'self'`,
  limit `img-src` to the schemes your images come from, and set `connect-src 'none'` if the
  page needs no network. The strict policy above is for a server that sends a fresh nonce.
- **Only what is on screen is in the page.** The editor draws the lines in view and a margin
  around them, not the whole document; this keeps long documents fast. Anything that reads the
  page's DOM sees only that part: the WebView's own find, copying the rendered HTML, and
  screen readers and other accessibility tools. Read the text with `editor.getDoc()`, and for
  find use the editor's own panel (Cmd/Ctrl+F, or `openSearchPanel(editor.view)` from
  `@codemirror/search`), which searches the whole document.

## Loaded on demand

The entry holds what every editor needs. The rest is fetched the first time a document needs
it, and never otherwise:

- **Mermaid** and the code for each diagram type, on the first `mermaid` code block of that type
  (never, with `diagrams: false`; not in the output at all, with the `no-diagrams` entry);
- **Temml**, on the first `$…$` or `$$…$$` formula;
- **a code language's grammar**, on the first fenced block in that language.

A document with none of these downloads only the entry and the chunks it shares.

## Sizes

Measured with the build above on the 0.1.0 package (minified, before compression):

- the output is about 230 files and 5.3 MB on disk, almost all of it lazy chunks that most pages
  never request;
- an editor that mounts on a plain document fetches the entry and the chunks it imports, about
  720 KB;
- the first diagram adds Mermaid's core and that diagram type, about 760 KB for a flowchart;
- the first formula adds Temml, about 210 KB; a code language adds from a few KB to about 50 KB;
- a document with a diagram, math and a code language fetches about 37 files, 1.7 MB.

Built from the `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` entry instead, the output is about 125
files and 1.9 MB on disk: no Mermaid chunks. What a page fetches is the same as above for
documents without a diagram (the entry is the same size; a document with math and a code
language fetches about 9 files, 950 KB). The saving is in what you build and deploy.

Serve the files compressed (gzip or brotli); this JavaScript shrinks to roughly a third. The
chunk names carry content hashes, so chunks can be cached for a long time; `editor.js` keeps its
name and should be revalidated.

# Fidelity

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/

Lossless round-trip: open a Markdown file and save it without editing, and the file is byte-for-byte what it was.

Most rich Markdown editors parse your file into a tree and write a new file out of that tree when
you save. That new file says the same thing in the editor's own style: your `_emphasis_` comes
back as `*emphasis*`, your `+` list as `-`, your setext heading as `#`, and some constructs, such
as frontmatter or callouts, can come back as something else.

This editor edits the text itself. What you typed changes, and the rest of the file stays as you
wrote it.

## The claim

This is the whole claim. Every sentence is backed by a test:

> OpenMarkdown edits your Markdown source text directly; it never rebuilds the file from a document tree. Open and save without editing, and the file is byte-for-byte what it was: line endings (LF / CRLF), BOM, final newline, whitespace, tabs, escapes and Unicode spelling untouched. When you edit, only what you touched changes, with a few exceptions, each pinned by a test: a table you edit (or click into a cell of) is re-aligned as a whole when you leave it — alignment, cell text and escapes kept; table commands rewrite that table the same way; indenting a list item or pressing Enter in a numbered list renumbers the affected items; Enter in a list item drops trailing spaces before the cursor; a file with mixed line endings gets uniform ones once you edit it; typing on a lone blank line between two blocks adds a line break after that line, so the block below stays separate.

The claim is about the file, so it holds when your host reads and writes the file with
`openMarkdownFile` and `saveMarkdownFile`. The editor keeps the document as a string in `\n` with
no BOM; these two keep what the string does not carry:

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const file = openMarkdownFile(bytes); // the file as read, a Uint8Array
const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, createEditorState({ doc: file.text }));

const out = saveMarkdownFile(editor.getDoc(), file); // the bytes to write
```

- **Strict UTF-8.** Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 throw `InvalidUtf8Error` (its `code` is
  `"INVALID_UTF8"`). Refuse to open the file: a lenient decode would replace the bad bytes with
  U+FFFD, and the next save would write that damage to disk.
- **Unedited, the original bytes.** While `editor.getDoc()` equals `file.text`, `saveMarkdownFile`
  returns `file.bytes`: BOM, line endings (LF, CRLF, lone CR, or a mix of them), a missing final
  newline and Unicode spelling exactly as they were.
- **Edited, the file's conventions.** The BOM is written back if there was one, and every line
  break is written as the file's dominant ending (`file.ending`: the most frequent one; on a tie,
  the one that comes first). A file with mixed line endings gets uniform ones once you edit it.

A host that does its own decoding has to keep the same three rules for the claim to hold. The
OpenMarkdown app keeps them in its own (Rust) file layer. The
[save-load example](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/) uses the two functions.

## Check it yourself

Run any Markdown file of yours through the package: open it, put it in an editor state, and save
it without editing. Save this as `roundtrip.mjs` and run `node roundtrip.mjs notes.md`:

```js roundtrip-check
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createEditorState, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const bytes = readFileSync(process.argv[2]);
const file = openMarkdownFile(bytes);
const state = createEditorState({ doc: file.text }); // in the editor, no edits
const saved = saveMarkdownFile(state.doc.toString(), file);

console.log(Buffer.compare(bytes, saved) === 0 ? "byte-identical" : "changed");
```

For a UTF-8 file it prints `byte-identical` (other bytes throw `InvalidUtf8Error`, see above).
The editor's own test suite runs this exact script on every test run
(`src/editor/roundtripCheck.gate.test.ts` in the editor's repository), over a test file of valid
but unusual Markdown (`fixtures/roundtrip/`: setext headings, `+` lists, reference links, odd
YAML, unaligned tables, NFD Unicode, trailing spaces, tabs) and its CRLF, BOM, mixed line ending,
lone CR and final newline variants.

In a browser, the [live demo](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/demo/) shows the same thing: its
developer panel says `0 bytes changed` until you type.

## What the exceptions look like

Edit one cell of a table whose columns are not aligned, and the whole table is re-aligned. Column
alignment colons, cell text and `\|` escapes are kept. This is the real diff from the comparison
below, after changing `22` to `23`:

```diff
-| Left | Center | Right |
-|:-----|:------:|------:|
-| `a\|b` | pipe \| escaped | 1 |
-|uneven|  cell | 23 |
+| Left   | Center          | Right |
+| :----- | :-------------: | ----: |
+| `a\|b` | pipe \| escaped | 1     |
+| uneven | cell            | 23    |
```

A table that is already aligned is left alone. Nothing else in the file moves.

## Compared with other editors

We opened the same 56-line Markdown file in six embeddable editors (their npm packages, in
headless Chromium), saved it without editing, then changed one word and saved again:

| Editor | Open → save, no edit | Change one word → save |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **@openmarkdown-dev/editor** (CodeMirror 6) | byte-identical | only that word changed |
| **Atomic Editor** (CodeMirror 6) | byte-identical | only that word changed |
| Milkdown Crepe (ProseMirror) | 13 of 22 tracked features changed | the same 30 changed lines, plus the word |
| Toast UI Editor (ProseMirror) | 15 of 22 changed | the same changes, plus the word |
| Tiptap + `@tiptap/markdown` (ProseMirror) | 17 of 22 changed | the same changes, plus the word |
| MDXEditor (Lexical) | refused the file (reference links); 13 of 19 changed without them | the edit was lost on the full file |

Atomic Editor ties with us here, because it is built the same way: the source is the document.
The difference is with editors that rebuild Markdown from a tree. When we edited one table cell,
both CodeMirror editors re-aligned that table. Ours kept the column alignment. Atomic's rewrote
the delimiter row to `| --- |` and lost it.

The method, an example diff, the run date and the caveats are on [the method page](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/method/).

# How we compared editors

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/method/

**Question:** if you open a Markdown file in an embeddable editor and save it, do you get your file
back?

**Run on 2026-11-04.** One test file (56 lines, 22 tracked features) went through six editors' npm
packages in headless Chromium, and we diffed what each one would save. The results include ones
that are bad for us; they are listed under [where OpenMarkdown did not win](#where-openmarkdown-did-not-win).

## The editors

| Editor | Package and version | Model | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenMarkdown | `@openmarkdown-dev/editor`, from source before its first npm release | CodeMirror 6, the source is the document | live-preview mode, no host |
| Atomic Editor | `@atomic-editor/editor` 0.6.2 | CodeMirror 6, the source is the document | defaults |
| Milkdown Crepe | `@milkdown/crepe` 7.22.3 | ProseMirror tree, serialized with remark | Crepe defaults (all features on) |
| MDXEditor | `@mdxeditor/editor` 4.3.3 | Lexical tree, serialized with mdast | headings, lists, quote, thematic break, link, link dialog, table, frontmatter, code block, image, Markdown shortcuts |
| Toast UI Editor | `@toast-ui/editor` 3.2.2 | ProseMirror tree, serialized with ToastMark | WYSIWYG mode, defaults otherwise |
| Tiptap | `@tiptap/core` + `@tiptap/markdown` 3.32.0 | ProseMirror tree, serialized with marked | StarterKit + TableKit + Markdown |

Every package was pinned to the newest release published at least two weeks before the run. All
six ran from npm in one Vite project, one page per editor, each loaded with its own Markdown import
and read back with its own export (`getDoc()` for OpenMarkdown, `getMarkdown()` for the others).
No public demo page was used.

## The tests

1. **Open → save.** Load the file, wait two seconds, then export with no input at all.
2. **One-word edit.** Double-click the word `quick` in a paragraph with a real mouse gesture, type
   `slow`, and export. The expected output is the file with only that word replaced.
3. **One table cell.** Click at the end of the cell `22`, press Backspace twice, type `23`, click
   into a paragraph to leave the table, and export.

**How a feature is scored.** Each of the 22 features is a verbatim snippet of the test file. A
feature counts as "changed" when that exact snippet is missing from the export. Each change was then
classified by reading the diff:

- **rewritten**: the meaning is the same and the syntax is different;
- **lost**: a GFM/CommonMark reader (or GitHub, for frontmatter and callouts) sees something
  different when the saved file is reopened.

## Results

| Editor | Open → save, no edit | Change one word → save | Then edit one table cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **OpenMarkdown** | byte-identical; 0 of 22 features changed | only the word changed | the whole table re-aligned (4 lines); alignment colons and `\|` kept |
| **Atomic Editor** | byte-identical; 0 of 22 | only the word changed | 2 lines changed; the delimiter row became `\| --- \| --- \| --- \|`, so column alignment is lost |
| Milkdown Crepe | 13 of 22 changed (2 lost, 11 rewritten); 30 diff lines | the same 30 lines plus the word | only the cell changed, in its already-rewritten table |
| MDXEditor | refused the file: a reference link stopped its parser, and the edit never reached its export | edit lost | n/a |
| MDXEditor, file without reference links | 13 of 19 changed (4 lost, 9 rewritten); 34 diff lines | the same plus the word | only the cell changed |
| Toast UI Editor | 15 of 22 changed (8 lost, 7 rewritten); 40 diff lines | the same plus the word | only the cell changed |
| Tiptap | 17 of 22 changed (3 lost, 14 rewritten); 41 diff lines | the same plus the word | only the cell changed |

"Diff lines" counts the `+` and `-` lines of `diff -u`. For each tree-based editor, the one-word
output is its open → save output with one word changed: a one-word edit saves the same 30 to 41
changed lines that opening the file already caused.

## Example diff

Milkdown, open then save with no edit. The YAML frontmatter comes back as a horizontal rule and a
heading:

```diff
----
+***
+
 title: Round-trip corpus
-tags: [a,b ,  c]
----
+tags: \[a,b ,  c]
+-----------------
```

## Feature by feature (open → save)

`kept` means the bytes are identical.

| Feature (source) | OpenMarkdown | Atomic | Milkdown | MDXEditor¹ | Toast UI | Tiptap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| frontmatter `---`…`---` | kept | kept | lost: `***` + paragraph + setext h2 | kept | lost | lost: `---` + `## title: …` |
| `*stars*` | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| `_underscores_` | kept | kept | kept | rewritten `*…*` | rewritten `*…*` | rewritten `*…*` |
| `__underscores__` | kept | kept | kept | rewritten `**…**` | rewritten `**…**` | rewritten `**…**` |
| setext h1 (`====`) | kept | kept | rewritten `# …` | rewritten `# …` | rewritten, underline shortened | rewritten `# …` |
| setext h2 (`----`) | kept | kept | rewritten `## …` | rewritten `## …` | rewritten `---` | rewritten `## …` |
| table delimiter row | kept | kept | rewritten (padded) | rewritten (padded) | rewritten | rewritten (padded) |
| table row with `` `a\|b` `` and `\|` | kept | kept | rewritten (padding; escapes kept) | rewritten (padding) | lost: the bare pipe splits the cell on reopen | rewritten (padding) |
| unpadded table row | kept | kept | rewritten | rewritten | rewritten | rewritten |
| `[the spec][spec]` | kept | kept | rewritten inline | refused | lost: never parsed as a link | rewritten inline |
| `[Collapsed][]` | kept | kept | rewritten inline | refused | lost | rewritten inline |
| link reference definitions | kept | kept | rewritten (deleted, inlined) | refused | lost | rewritten (deleted, inlined) |
| `+` list marker | kept | kept | rewritten `*` | rewritten `*` | rewritten `*` | rewritten `-` |
| `*` list marker | kept | kept | rewritten `-` | kept | kept | rewritten `-` |
| two adjacent lists stay two | kept | kept | kept | lost: merged into one list | lost: one list on reopen | lost: one list on reopen |
| ordered list starting at `3.` | kept | kept | kept | lost: renumbered `1.` | kept | kept |
| backslash hard break `\` | kept | kept | kept | lost: soft break | lost: lines glued | rewritten as two trailing spaces |
| trailing spaces (a hard break) | kept | kept | rewritten `\` | lost: soft break | lost: lines glued | rewritten (2 spaces) |
| HTML block `<div align="center">` | kept | kept | kept | kept | lost: glued into the previous paragraph | lost: `**HTML block**` |
| inline math `$E = mc^2$` | kept | kept | kept | rewritten `$E \= mc^2$` | kept | kept |
| callout `> [!NOTE]` | kept | kept | lost: `> \[!NOTE]` | lost: `> \[!NOTE]` | kept | lost: `> \[!NOTE\]` |
| CJK paragraph | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| `\*not emphasis\*` | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| final newline | kept | kept | kept | dropped | dropped | dropped |

¹ MDXEditor values are from the run without the reference-link section. With the full file, it
reports a parse error on the reference link and renders nothing after it.

## Caveats

- **Atomic Editor ties with us.** It is also built on CodeMirror and edits the text itself. The
  split here is editing the text against editing a tree, not us against everyone.
- **Table edits:** editing one cell in OpenMarkdown re-aligns that whole table (4 lines in this
  file). Atomic changes 2 lines there, but drops the column alignment.
- **The test file is ours.** It uses valid but less common syntax on purpose: setext headings, `+`
  lists, reference links. A file written in one canonical style (ATX headings, `-` lists, `**`,
  padded tables) loses much less in a tree editor. A fair summary is "tree editors normalize your
  style and lose some constructs", not "they corrupt everything".
- **Configuration matters.** Each tree-based editor can be extended with more plugins; some
  community plugins (frontmatter, for example) could fix some rows. Rewriting `_` / `__`, setext
  headings, list markers and table padding is a property of serializing a tree, not a missing
  plugin.
- **"Lost"** means a Markdown reader sees something different when the saved file is reopened;
  **"changed"** includes harmless rewrites like `_a_` to `*a*`.
- **One run per editor, in headless Chromium.** Results were identical across every run made while
  building the test (six full runs).
- **Single gestures.** The edit tests do not cover typing-heavy sessions, paste, undo or IME input.
- **The editor alone.** OpenMarkdown was run from its source before the first npm release. The
  app's disk layer (BOM, CRLF) is not involved for this LF, BOM-less file; the editor's own
  fidelity tests cover it separately.

## Where OpenMarkdown did not win

- **The tie with Atomic Editor** on open → save and on a prose edit. Do not read these results as
  "the one editor that keeps your file".
- **Table edits** rewrite more bytes than Atomic's (4 lines against 2), by design.
- **`\|` inside inline code in a table** displays as `a\|b` in OpenMarkdown. GFM reads that cell as
  `a|b`, and Milkdown, MDXEditor and Toast UI display it that way. The bytes are kept, but the
  display is wrong.
- **Double-click inside a table cell** first opens the cell editor and places the caret, where the
  other editors select the word. The table test uses click and Backspace for each editor, so the
  numbers above are not affected, but a user would notice it.

The round-trip test file and the test that runs it are in the editor's repository
(`fixtures/roundtrip/`, `src/editor/roundtripCheck.gate.test.ts`). The comparison harness and its
per-feature results are not public yet.

# InvalidUtf8Error

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/classes/invalidutf8error/

Thrown by `openMarkdownFile` when the bytes are not valid UTF-8. Refuse to
open the file in the editor: decoding it anyway would replace the bad bytes
with U+FFFD, and the next save would write that damage to disk. Recognise it
with `instanceof`, or by `code` (`"INVALID_UTF8"`) across bundles.

## Extends

- `Error`

## Constructors

### Constructor

> **new InvalidUtf8Error**(`options?`): `InvalidUtf8Error`

#### Parameters

##### options?

###### cause?

`unknown`

The decoder's own error.

#### Returns

`InvalidUtf8Error`

#### Overrides

`Error.constructor`

## Properties

### cause?

> `optional` **cause?**: `unknown`

#### Inherited from

`Error.cause`

***

### code

> `readonly` **code**: `"INVALID_UTF8"` = `"INVALID_UTF8"`

Always `"INVALID_UTF8"`.

***

### message

> **message**: `string`

#### Inherited from

`Error.message`

***

### name

> **name**: `string`

#### Inherited from

`Error.name`

***

### stack?

> `optional` **stack?**: `string`

#### Inherited from

`Error.stack`

***

### stackTraceLimit

> `static` **stackTraceLimit**: `number`

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

#### Inherited from

`Error.stackTraceLimit`

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

##### targetObject

`object`

##### constructorOpt?

`Function`

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

`Error.captureStackTrace`

***

### prepareStackTrace()

> `static` **prepareStackTrace**(`err`, `stackTraces`): `any`

#### Parameters

##### err

`Error`

##### stackTraces

`CallSite`[]

#### Returns

`any`

#### See

https://v8.dev/docs/stack-trace-api#customizing-stack-traces

#### Inherited from

`Error.prepareStackTrace`

# configureEditorEnvironment

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/configureeditorenvironment/

> **configureEditorEnvironment**(`env`): `void`

Provide the window-wide capabilities (`EditorEnvironment`). Call once at
startup, before the first editor mounts; a later call replaces the whole
environment. Optional: without it the editor is light, English, and has no
clipboard, external-link, spelling or host-key behaviour.

## Parameters

### env

[`EditorEnvironment`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorenvironment/)

## Returns

`void`

# createEditorState

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/createeditorstate/

> **createEditorState**(`options`): `EditorState`

Build an editor state: the document, caret, undo history, folds and mode,
with the whole editor (live preview, structure keys, find, folding, tables,
math, diagrams) installed. Show it with `mountEditor`; a host with several
documents keeps one state per document and swaps them into one view
(`editor.view.setState(state)`, then `editor.syncAmbient()`).

## Parameters

### options

[`EditorStateOptions`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorstateoptions/)

## Returns

`EditorState`

# mountEditor

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/mounteditor/

> **mountEditor**(`parent`, `state`): [`MarkdownEditor`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowneditor/)

Mount `state` (from `createEditorState`) in a new editor view appended to
`parent`, following the environment's color scheme while it lives. Returns
the editor handle; call its `destroy` when done.

## Parameters

### parent

`HTMLElement`

### state

`EditorState`

## Returns

[`MarkdownEditor`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowneditor/)

# openMarkdownFile

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/openmarkdownfile/

> **openMarkdownFile**(`bytes`): [`MarkdownFile`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdownfile/)

Open a Markdown file's bytes for the editor. Decodes strict UTF-8 (invalid
bytes throw `InvalidUtf8Error`; nothing is replaced), notes and strips a
leading BOM, detects the line endings (LF, CRLF, lone CR, or a mix) and turns
them into `\n`, and keeps a copy of the original bytes. Save with
`saveMarkdownFile`.

## Parameters

### bytes

`Uint8Array`

The file as read from disk, a network response or a file input.

## Returns

[`MarkdownFile`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdownfile/)

The text to edit, and what saving needs to write the file back.

## Throws

InvalidUtf8Error when `bytes` is not valid UTF-8.

# saveMarkdownFile

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/savemarkdownfile/

> **saveMarkdownFile**(`doc`, `file`): `Uint8Array`

The bytes to write for the editor's document. Unedited (`doc` equals
`file.text`), they are the original bytes, exactly. Edited, they are `doc`
encoded as UTF-8 with the file's BOM put back and every line break written
as `file.ending`; a file with mixed line endings gets uniform ones.

## Parameters

### doc

`string`

The document to save, usually `editor.getDoc()`.

### file

[`MarkdownFile`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdownfile/)

What `openMarkdownFile` returned for this file.

## Returns

`Uint8Array`

The file's bytes.

# EditorEnvironment

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorenvironment/

The editor environment: window-wide capabilities the host provides once per
page with `configureEditorEnvironment`. Per-document needs go through
`EditorHost` instead.

Every member is optional: what the host leaves out is switched off quietly —
no error, no notice, no fallback of the editor's own. An editor mounted with
no environment configured at all is light, English, editable, and has no
copy, external-link, spelling or host-key behaviour.

## Properties

### colorScheme?

> `optional` **colorScheme?**: `object`

The window's light / dark scheme: its value now, and a subscription to changes (returns the unsubscribe).

#### current()

##### Returns

[`ColorScheme`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/colorscheme/)

#### subscribe()

##### Parameters

###### cb

(`scheme`) => `void`

##### Returns

() => `void`

***

### copyText?

Put `text` on the clipboard (code-block copy button). The host reports success / failure itself.

#### Parameters

##### text

`string`

#### Returns

`unknown`

***

### handleKey?

> `optional` **handleKey?**: (`view`, `event`) => `boolean`

Offered every key the editor's keymap sees, before CodeMirror's defaults:
return true when the host ran a binding for it (the key is consumed).

#### Parameters

##### view

`EditorView`

##### event

`KeyboardEvent`

#### Returns

`boolean`

***

### language?

> `optional` **language?**: `"zh"` \| `"ja"` \| `"ko"` \| `"en"`

The language of the editor's own UI words. Read whenever a word is drawn,
so set it before the first editor mounts; already-drawn words do not redraw
on a change. Left out, or not one the editor ships: English.

***

### openExternal?

> `optional` **openExternal?**: (`url`) => `unknown`

Open an external (non-file) link target, e.g. Cmd/Ctrl+click on `https://…`. The host owns the policy.

#### Parameters

`string`

#### Returns

`unknown`

***

### refusedLink?

> `optional` **refusedLink?**: (`url`, `scheme`) => `unknown`

The editor refused to follow a script-capable link (`javascript:` /
`vbscript:` / `data:` …, however obfuscated); `scheme` is the
scheme as a browser reads it. For telling the user only: the URL MUST NOT
be opened. Absent: the refusal is silent.

#### Parameters

##### url

`string`

`string`

#### Returns
